<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|HOLY weeke. 208|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XXIII.}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=23|verse=17}}† And he of necessitie had to release vnto them vpon the feast day, one. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=18}}† But the vvhole multitude together cried out, saying, Dispatch him, and release vs Barabbas. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=19}}† vvho vvas for a certaine sedition made in the citie and murder, cast into prison. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=20}}† And Pilate againe spake to them, desirous to release {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=21}}† But they cried againe, saying, Crucifie, crucifie him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=22}}† And he the third time said to them, VVhy, vvhat euil hath this man done? I finde no cause of death in him. I vvil correct him therfore and let him goe. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=23}}† But they vvere instant vvith loude voices requiring that he might be crucified. And their voices preuailed. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=24}}† And Pilate adiudged their petition to be done. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=25}}† And he released vnto them him that for murder and sedition had been cast into prison, vvhom they demaunded: but {{sc|Iesvs}} he deliuered to their pleasure.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=26}}† And vvhen they led him, they tooke one Simon of Cyréne comming from the countrie: and they laid the crosse vpon him to carie after {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=27}}† And there folovved him a great multitude of people, and of vvomen vvhich bevvailed and lamented him. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=28}}† But {{sc|Iesvs}} turning to them, said, Daughters of Hierusalem, vveepe not vpon me, but vveepe vpon your selues, and vpon your children. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=29}}† For behold the daies shal come, vvherein they vvil say, Blessed are the barren, and the vvombes that haue not borne, and the pappes that haue not giuen sucke. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=30}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Os. 10, 8.''}}* ''Then shal they begin to say to the mountaines, Fal vpon vs: and to the hilles, Couer vs''. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=31}}† For if in the greene wood they doe these things, in the drie vvhat shal be done?

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=32}}† And there vvere led also other tvvo malefactours vvith him, to be executed. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=33}}† And after they came to the place vvhich is called Caluarie, there they crucified him: and the theeues, one on the right hand, and the other on the left. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=34}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said, Father, {{sup|‖}} forgiue them, for they knovv not vvhat they doe. But they deuiding his garments, did cast lottes.

{{verse|chapter=23|verse=35}}† And the people stoode {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''`beholding'',}}`expecting', and the princes vvith them derided him, saying, Others he hath saued, let him saue him self, if this be Christ, the elect of God. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=36}}† And the souldiars also mocked him comming to him, and offering him vinegre, {{verse|chapter=23|verse=37}}† saying, If thou be the king of the Ievves, saue thy self. {{verse|chapter=23|verse=38}}† And there vvas also a superscription vvritten ouer him in Greeke, and Latine, and Hebrevv letters:<noinclude>{{rh|||{{sc|This}}}}</noinclude>
